descriptor.title: We may have exposed customer information
descriptor.introduction: What must we do after customer data is exposed? A fictional business decision with a reviewed action document.

strategies.title: Advice tested against business and legal risks
strategies.input_summary: Fictional Copper Ledger discovers an exposed cloud export at 9 a.m. September 20, 2026. It contains 2,000 customer records, including names, email addresses and password-reset tokens; a separate column may contain bank-account numbers for some customers, but the security team has not verified it. Residency flags list 1,200 California and 800 New York residents and may be stale. Access logs show one unknown IP downloaded an object overnight; encryption and key-access facts remain unresolved. The public link was disabled at 10 a.m. Contracts require prompt notice of security incidents but their exact timing provisions have not been collected. The CEO wants to announce “no sensitive data was accessed” by noon.
assumptions: All business facts and organizations in this scenario are fictional.
Missing facts must remain unresolved rather than assumed favorable.

initial.response_text:
## Recommendation
Since the link is disabled, tell customers no sensitive data was accessed and wait for confirmed misuse before considering notices. We have a standard 72-hour deadline everywhere.

## Proposed action
Proceed on that recommendation using the supplied business objective; this initial draft has not yet addressed the opposing critique.

revised.response_text:
## Recommendation
Contain and preserve evidence now, activate the incident team, and use an accurate holding statement. Treat notification as a parallel legal workstream, not something postponed until fraud appears. Counsel should determine each applicable trigger, deadline, recipient and content requirement from verified facts and current authority, including contractual and sector obligations.

## Risks
The record does not establish the exact exposed fields, token usability, residency, encryption protection or attacker access to keys. These facts can change the notification analysis. A public claim of no sensitive access would exceed the evidence and may need correction. California and New York reporting thresholds and requirements differ; the matrix gives conditional statutory periods, not a conclusion that every listed record triggers notice.

## Options
Use a narrow factual holding statement while forensic work continues. Deliver contractually required incident information when due, distinguishing it from statutory breach notices. Prepare conditional state notice drafts in parallel, updating them as facts resolve. Delaying all work until misuse is proven risks missing obligations and leaves customers unable to protect accounts.

## Next Steps
Security: preserve cloud logs and the original export under controlled access, revoke exposed tokens, scope downloads and confirm fields/encryption. Legal: collect customer contracts, insurance conditions and statutory sources; create a deadline matrix with discovery/awareness dates and escalation owners. Communications: approve a single factual update channel. Privacy: validate residency and minimize further handling of the exposed records.

## Secondary Deliverable
**Triage checklist and notification decision matrix**
Immediate: disable public access; invalidate usable tokens; preserve logs; identify the downloaded object; restrict incident evidence to the response team.
California row: confirm covered data and acquisition first. Section1798.82(a) generally sets30 calendar days from discovery/notification, with specified delay grounds; maintainer-to-owner notice is immediate under(b). If more than500 residents require notice, submit the AG sample within15 calendar days after consumer notice under(f).
New York row: confirm private information and unauthorized access/acquisition. Section899-aa(2) requires the most expedient notice without unreasonable delay and within30 days after discovery, subject to the statutory law-enforcement exception. Map owner/maintainer roles and agency recipients separately. If September20 starts the applicable30-day clock, provisionally calendar October20; counsel must validate triggers and earlier duties today.
Contract row: legal owner obtains each incident clause, starts its required clock and records recipient/method. Sector/insurance row: identify additional duties independently.
**Holding statement:** “We identified and disabled an unintended public link to a customer-data export on September 20. We are investigating the information involved and access to it, and have taken steps to secure affected systems. We will provide further information and any required notices as facts are confirmed.”
Do not add “no sensitive data” or “no access” without evidence.

## Source boundary
Law-as-of preparation: September 20, 2026. Source summaries and links are in the input packet. This draft does not establish citation currency or attorney approval.
